rationale.usefulness: Prompt-controlled transcripts, translation, speaker tags and word timing have direct educational and editorial value. The report offers specific reviewed-transcript and navigation workflows while documenting a substantial BF16 deployment, a provider-priced route and task-specific language limits.
rationale.impact: Combining multiple recorded-audio tasks with adaptation resources can simplify a meaningful class of speech applications. It is still a domain-specific release, with unreplicated benchmark claims, a substantial memory requirement and unresolved launch-day quantized distribution limiting immediate broader impact.
rationale.novelty: The integrated promptable speech model, speaker-aware path, timestamp head and explicit transcript-convention data provide useful differentiation. Transcription, translation, diarization and speech-language modeling already exist, so the evidence supports a strong integration improvement rather than a wholly new capability.
rationale.maturity: The model card, 67.5 GB BF16 artifact listing, one-H100 quickstart and serving guide are concrete. New-release status, inconsistent FP8/NVFP4 availability, development-serving limitations and the absence of execution or quality tests prevent a stronger readiness score.
rationale.openness: OpenMDW-1.1 weights, public serving/training tooling and Granary label manifests offer substantial inspection and adaptation access. The manifests omit source audio and the full training mixture; subset and upstream licenses differ, and highest-throughput serving optimizations are not yet in the open release.

concerns: No publication-blocking factual issue found. The report correctly retains the 404-route uncertainty, differing WER snapshots, offline-only boundary and separation of active parameter count from total checkpoint size.
No external leaderboard, transcription quality, timestamp accuracy, hosted billing or complete training reproduction was independently validated.
